title: Positive component degrees characterize ampleness on a proper curve
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] with topological dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $1$. Let $\mathcal M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For each one-dimensional irreducible component $C$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] of the reduced scheme $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme], let $\widetilde C\to C$ be its normalization [def-sc-normalization]. Then $\mathcal M$ is ample on $X$ in the absolute sense of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] if and only if the degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] of the pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] of $\mathcal M$ to every $\widetilde C$ is positive. Zero-dimensional components impose no condition.

source.place: Tag 0B5Y, lemma-ampleness-in-terms-of-degrees-components; normalization is finite and birational by Tag 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic), and its degree-one pullback preserves degree by Tag 0AYZ (lemma-degree-pullback-map-proper-curves).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-proper-curve-normalized-component-cover] to $X$: write $f:Z\to X$ for the finite surjective map from the finite disjoint union of the normalized one-dimensional reduced components $\widetilde C_i$ and the isolated reduced point components $P_j$. It supplies that $Z$ is proper over $k$, every $\widetilde C_i$ is integral and proper of dimension one, and every $P_j$ is integral of dimension zero. The reduced induced components are exactly those of $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ occurring in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0B5Y, lemma-ampleness-in-terms-of-degrees-components, proof: finite surjective component cover (details omitted); replace each curve component by its normalization using Tag 0BXR, lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian: its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$, both finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Thus [lem-trf-finite-surjective-ample-reflection] applies over $R=k$ to the finite surjective $k$-morphism $f$ between the proper $k$-schemes $Z$ and $X$. It gives $\mathcal M$ ample on $X$ if and only if $f^*\mathcal M$ is ample on $Z$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], $f^*\mathcal M$ is invertible. Apply [lem-trf-finite-coproduct-ample-with-points] to $Z$: its ampleness is equivalent to ampleness on every $\widetilde C_i$, with the point restrictions automatically ample. If $h_i:\widetilde C_i\to X$ is the normalization followed by the component inclusion, the same pullback theorem identifies the restriction of $f^*\mathcal M$ to this summand with $h_i^*\mathcal M$, and supplies its invertibility.

source.place: Tag 01PS, definition-ample, applied to a finite disjoint union; the isolated-point summands in Varieties Tag 0B5Y, lemma-ampleness-in-terms-of-degrees-components.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-proper-integral-curve-ample-degree] to each proper integral dimension-one $k$-scheme $\widetilde C_i$ and its invertible module $h_i^*\mathcal M$. Its ampleness is equivalent to $\deg_k(h_i^*\mathcal M)>0$, exactly the normalization degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] in the statement. Composing the equivalences proves both implications. When there are no curve components the condition is vacuous; the point-summand result still applies. When $X$ is empty so is $Z$, and the affine-locus definition [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] and the degree condition are both vacuous.

lean.statement: theorem isAmple_iff_normalizedComponentDegree_pos (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsProper (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (M : X.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] : IsAmple X M ↔ ∀ (C : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral C] (i : C ⟶ X), IsClosedImmersion i → Set.range i ∈ irreducibleComponents X → topologicalKrullDim C = 1 → 0 < @Scheme.Modules.degree k _ C.normalization ⟨C.fromNormalization ≫ i ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of k))⟩ ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (C.fromNormalization ≫ i)).obj M)
